Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher's fortunes turned in 1772 with the ouster of _____ by his deputy Abu al-Dhahab
Daher al-Umar.fact: Daher allied with Egypt's mamluk strongman, Ali Bey, and the Shias of southern Lebanon. Daher's fortunes turned in 1772 with the ouster of Ali Bey by his deputy Abu al-Dhahab.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: By 1773, Daher had 272 children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren, according to the contemporary _____
Daher al-Umar.fact: By 1773, Daher had 272 children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren, according to the contemporary Sauveur Lusignan.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In 1738, Daher led a 1,500-strong force which defeated Ahmad and gained control over his fortress Jiddin and its dependencies, _____ and Tarshiha
Daher al-Umar.fact: In 1738, Daher led a 1,500-strong force which defeated Ahmad and gained control over his fortress Jiddin and its dependencies, Abu Sinan and Tarshiha.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Sulayman Pasha al-Azm became governor in 1734 and opposed Daher's buildup of power on the borders of his province and encroachments into _____
Daher al-Umar.fact: Sulayman Pasha al-Azm became governor in 1734 and opposed Daher's buildup of power on the borders of his province and encroachments into Nablus Sanjak.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Sulayman Pasha resumed the operation after his return to _____ from the Hajj in July 1743
Daher al-Umar.fact: Sulayman Pasha resumed the operation after his return to Damascus from the Hajj in July 1743. The following fourteen years were characterized by peace between Daher and Damascus, partly because As'ad Pasha was dissuaded by his uncle's unsuccessful experience and preoccupied with domestic affairs.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In late 1757, the _____ and Sardiyya tribes launched an assault on the Hajj caravan on its return to Syria
Daher al-Umar.fact: In late 1757, the Banu Sakhr and Sardiyya tribes launched an assault on the Hajj caravan on its return to Syria.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In 1730, Daher took over _____ and by c
Daher al-Umar.fact: In 1730, Daher took over Tiberias and by c.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Around 1698, _____ effectively became the tax collector of Safed
Daher al-Umar.fact: His father, Umar, was the sheikh of the Zayadina (sing. Around 1698, Umar effectively became the tax collector of Safed.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In 1707, Daher was entangled in a brawl, killing a man from _____
Daher al-Umar.fact: In 1707, Daher was entangled in a brawl, killing a man from Tiberias. Sa'd consequently moved the family to Arraba, a village between the commercial centers of Tiberias, Safed and Nazareth but away from the main highways.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In 1737 and 1738, Daher launched raids into the Jawlan (Golan) and Hauran, and attacked _____ city
Daher al-Umar.fact: In 1737 and 1738, Daher launched raids into the Jawlan (Golan) and Hauran, and attacked Damascus city. The imperial government in Constantinople determined Daher was a threat to the all-important Hajj pilgrim caravan to Mecca, which was annually marshaled in Damascus and traditionally led by its governor.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: With imperial sanction, _____ launched an abortive attack against Daher in 1738
Daher al-Umar.fact: More alarming to Sulayman Pasha than Daher's activities in Palestine were his incursions east of the Jordan River. With imperial sanction, Sulayman Pasha launched an abortive attack against Daher in 1738.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In 1743, Daher executed his cousin _____ to remove him as a rival for influence in Acre
Daher al-Umar.fact: To earn the government's favor, he purchased the looted goods of the caravan from the Bedouin, including the decorated banners representing the Islamic prophet Muhammad and the sovereignty of the sultan, and restored them to Sultan Mustafa III (Osman III had died on 30 October). In 1743, Daher executed his cousin Muhammad to remove him as a rival for influence in Acre.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher took _____ by force, probably in 1744, and killed its multazim
Daher al-Umar.fact: Control of Acre would greatly improve his business potential, and peace with Damascus enabled Daher to focus his military resources against the port. In 1743, Daher executed his cousin Muhammad to remove him as a rival for influence in Acre.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: After mobilizing its ulema (Muslim scholars) and qadi (Islamic head judge) to petition the sultan on his behalf, in July _____, Daher was formally appointed the multazim of Acre
Daher al-Umar.fact: After mobilizing its ulema (Muslim scholars) and qadi (Islamic head judge) to petition the sultan on his behalf, in July 1746, Daher was formally appointed the multazim of Acre.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: After completing a wall around Acre and other public works, Daher made it his new headquarters around _____, relocating there from Deir Hanna
Daher al-Umar.fact: After completing a wall around Acre and other public works, Daher made it his new headquarters around 1750, relocating there from Deir Hanna.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Afterward, Daher confiscated five nearby villages, Julis, Mazra'a, Makr, _____, and Sumayriyya, as personal estates, which he also developed
Daher al-Umar.fact: Afterward, Daher confiscated five nearby villages, Julis, Mazra'a, Makr, Judayda, and Sumayriyya, as personal estates, which he also developed.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: He installed water mills on the Na'aman River south of Acre and the Ga'aton River north of the city, both part of the 16th-century waqf (endowment) of _____ to which he paid a fixed amount yearly
Daher al-Umar.fact: He installed water mills on the Na'aman River south of Acre and the Ga'aton River north of the city, both part of the 16th-century waqf (endowment) of Sinan Pasha to which he paid a fixed amount yearly.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In _____, Daher expanded his holdings southward, along Palestine's northern coastal plain, taking control of Haifa, Tira, and Tantura, and the adjoining Mount Carmel
Daher al-Umar.fact: In 1757, Daher expanded his holdings southward, along Palestine's northern coastal plain, taking control of Haifa, Tira, and Tantura, and the adjoining Mount Carmel.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: _____–1771), attempted to return the port to Damascene authority
Daher al-Umar.fact: 1760–1771), attempted to return the port to Damascene authority.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Acting on Uthman Pasha's request, the governor of Sidon, Nu'man Pasha, dispatched 30 Maghrebi mercenaries on a vessel captained by a Frenchman to capture Haifa in May _____
Daher al-Umar.fact: Acting on Uthman Pasha's request, the governor of Sidon, Nu'man Pasha, dispatched 30 Maghrebi mercenaries on a vessel captained by a Frenchman to capture Haifa in May 1761.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: The issue over Haifa's annexation was smoothed over with the assistance of _____, a Constantinople-based official with friendly ties to Daher
Daher al-Umar.fact: The issue over Haifa's annexation was smoothed over with the assistance of Yaqub Agha, a Constantinople-based official with friendly ties to Daher. Yaqub Agha had a high-ranking official, the kizlar agha (chief eunuch) Sulayman Agha, revoke the imperial order sanctioning Uthman Pasha's attempt to capture the Haifa coast.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Yaqub Agha had a high-ranking official, the kizlar agha (chief eunuch) _____, revoke the imperial order sanctioning Uthman Pasha's attempt to capture the Haifa coast
Daher al-Umar.fact: Yaqub Agha had a high-ranking official, the kizlar agha (chief eunuch) Sulayman Agha, revoke the imperial order sanctioning Uthman Pasha's attempt to capture the Haifa coast.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Besides support from elements of the _____, Daher's sons maintained separate power bases, largely derived from their mothers' families, and formed alliances with other local powers
Daher al-Umar.fact: Besides support from elements of the Zayadina, Daher's sons maintained separate power bases, largely derived from their mothers' families, and formed alliances with other local powers.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In _____, Daher detected a plot by his son Uthman and brother Sa'd, hitherto his chief adviser, to eliminate him
Daher al-Umar.fact: In 1761, Daher detected a plot by his son Uthman and brother Sa'd, hitherto his chief adviser, to eliminate him.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher turned _____ to kill Sa'd, offering him control of Shefa-Amr in exchange
Daher al-Umar.fact: In 1761, Daher detected a plot by his son Uthman and brother Sa'd, hitherto his chief adviser, to eliminate him. Daher turned Uthman to kill Sa'd, offering him control of Shefa-Amr in exchange.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In May _____, Uthman renewed his rebellion but was again defeated
Daher al-Umar.fact: In May 1766, Uthman renewed his rebellion but was again defeated.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Mediation by Isma'il _____ of Hasbaya culminated in a peace summit reconciling Daher and Uthman
Daher al-Umar.fact: Mediation by Isma'il Shihab of Hasbaya culminated in a peace summit reconciling Daher and Uthman.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In September _____, a conflict between Daher and his son Ali, who controlled Safed, broke out over Ali's attempts to obtain the key fortress of Deir Hanna
Daher al-Umar.fact: In September 1767, a conflict between Daher and his son Ali, who controlled Safed, broke out over Ali's attempts to obtain the key fortress of Deir Hanna. The disputes were settled by December 1767, with Daher ceding Deir Hanna for token payment.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: The disputes were settled by December _____, with Daher ceding Deir Hanna for token payment
Daher al-Umar.fact: In September 1767, a conflict between Daher and his son Ali, who controlled Safed, broke out over Ali's attempts to obtain the key fortress of Deir Hanna. The disputes were settled by December 1767, with Daher ceding Deir Hanna for token payment.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: The rebellions by Daher's sons were nearly always backed by the governor of Damascus, _____, in a bid to sustain internal dissent and undermine Daher
Daher al-Umar.fact: The rebellions by Daher's sons were nearly always backed by the governor of Damascus, Uthman Pasha, in a bid to sustain internal dissent and undermine Daher. The latter lodged complaints to the imperial government about Uthman Pasha's support for his rebellious sons at least once in 1765.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: The latter lodged complaints to the imperial government about Uthman Pasha's support for his rebellious sons at least once in _____
Daher al-Umar.fact: The latter lodged complaints to the imperial government about Uthman Pasha's support for his rebellious sons at least once in 1765.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher received the support of the governor of Sidon, _____ al-Azm, an opponent of Uthman Pasha who sought to restore the Azms to office in Damascus
Daher al-Umar.fact: Daher received the support of the governor of Sidon, Muhammad Pasha al-Azm, an opponent of Uthman Pasha who sought to restore the Azms to office in Damascus.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Their territory was wedged between the Shihabs in _____ and the Zayadina in northern Palestine
Daher al-Umar.fact: Their territory was wedged between the Shihabs in Mount Lebanon and the Zayadina in northern Palestine.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In _____, Nassar, the sheikh of the Ali al-Saghirs, the strongest Metawali clan, assisted government forces in their campaign against Daher
Daher al-Umar.fact: In 1743, Nassar, the sheikh of the Ali al-Saghirs, the strongest Metawali clan, assisted government forces in their campaign against Daher.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Around _____, Nassar's successor, his son Daher al-Nassar, called for Daher's backing against the Shihabs, who had earlier killed hundreds of Metawali villagers and sacked villages in Jabal Amil
Daher al-Umar.fact: Around 1750, Nassar's successor, his son Daher al-Nassar, called for Daher's backing against the Shihabs, who had earlier killed hundreds of Metawali villagers and sacked villages in Jabal Amil.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher al-_____ died that year and was succeeded by his brother, Nasif al-Nassar
Daher al-Umar.fact: In 1743, Nassar, the sheikh of the Ali al-Saghirs, the strongest Metawali clan, assisted government forces in their campaign against Daher. Around 1750, Nassar's successor, his son Daher al-Nassar, called for Daher's backing against the Shihabs, who had earlier killed hundreds of Metawali villagers and sacked villages in Jabal Amil.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Nasif and the other Metawali sheikhs backed Daher's son Uthman during his rebellion against him in _____, and then his other son Ali in 1767
Daher al-Umar.fact: Nasif and the other Metawali sheikhs backed Daher's son Uthman during his rebellion against him in 1766, and then his other son Ali in 1767. After a series of clashes, the two sides fought at the village of Tarbikha on 6 October 1766, with Sabbagh claiming the battle ended in Daher's victory and Rukayni claiming Nasif as the decisive victor.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: After a series of clashes, the two sides fought at the village of Tarbikha on 6 October _____, with Sabbagh claiming the battle ended in Daher's victory and Rukayni claiming Nasif as the decisive vict
Daher al-Umar.fact: Nasif and the other Metawali sheikhs backed Daher's son Uthman during his rebellion against him in 1766, and then his other son Ali in 1767. After a series of clashes, the two sides fought at the village of Tarbikha on 6 October 1766, with Sabbagh claiming the battle ended in Daher's victory and Rukayni claiming Nasif as the decisive victor.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Amid the conflict, Daher captured the fortified _____ villages of Bassa and Yaroun on the borders of Zaydani territory
Daher al-Umar.fact: Nasif and the other Metawali sheikhs backed Daher's son Uthman during his rebellion against him in 1766, and then his other son Ali in 1767. Amid the conflict, Daher captured the fortified Metawali villages of Bassa and Yaroun on the borders of Zaydani territory.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Thereafter, Daher's _____ mercenaries supposedly employed a ruse by capturing two of Nasif's yong sons from Nasif's headquarters, the Tebnine castle, compelling Nasif to negotiate terms
Daher al-Umar.fact: Thereafter, Daher's Maghrebi mercenaries supposedly employed a ruse by capturing two of Nasif's yong sons from Nasif's headquarters, the Tebnine castle, compelling Nasif to negotiate terms.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: This account is considered a local legend by the historian _____, and Philipp deems Rukayni more reliable for these events
Daher al-Umar.fact: This account is considered a local legend by the historian Stefan Winter, and Philipp deems Rukayni more reliable for these events.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Despite their conflict, Daher and the _____ shared an interest in limiting Sidon's power and keeping the Druze emirs at bay
Daher al-Umar.fact: Despite their conflict, Daher and the Metawalis shared an interest in limiting Sidon's power and keeping the Druze emirs at bay. By its terms, Daher kept control of Bassa and Yaroun, represented the Metawalis in their fiscal relations with Sidon, and reduced their tax obligations by a quarter.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: By its terms, Daher kept control of Bassa and Yaroun, represented the _____ in their fiscal relations with Sidon, and reduced their tax obligations by a quarter
Daher al-Umar.fact: Despite their conflict, Daher and the Metawalis shared an interest in limiting Sidon's power and keeping the Druze emirs at bay. By its terms, Daher kept control of Bassa and Yaroun, represented the Metawalis in their fiscal relations with Sidon, and reduced their tax obligations by a quarter.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher backed the _____ in any confrontation with the Druze, in return for the Metawalis' military support
Daher al-Umar.fact: Despite their conflict, Daher and the Metawalis shared an interest in limiting Sidon's power and keeping the Druze emirs at bay. By its terms, Daher kept control of Bassa and Yaroun, represented the Metawalis in their fiscal relations with Sidon, and reduced their tax obligations by a quarter.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher's son Uthman secured a treaty between Daher and Nasif, dated by Rukayni to 24 November _____
Daher al-Umar.fact: Daher's son Uthman secured a treaty between Daher and Nasif, dated by Rukayni to 24 November 1767.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: He effectively became the multazim of _____, greatly expanding his territory
Daher al-Umar.fact: He effectively became the multazim of Jabal Amil, greatly expanding his territory.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: The backing of thousands of _____ fighters significantly boosted Daher's military potential, and the Metawalis "remained faithful allies ..
Daher al-Umar.fact: By its terms, Daher kept control of Bassa and Yaroun, represented the Metawalis in their fiscal relations with Sidon, and reduced their tax obligations by a quarter. Daher backed the Metawalis in any confrontation with the Druze, in return for the Metawalis' military support.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: to the end", in _____'s words, participating in fifteen subsequent campaigns against Daher's foes
Daher al-Umar.fact: to the end", in Philipp's words, participating in fifteen subsequent campaigns against Daher's foes.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher was at the peak of his power, having consolidated his alliance with the _____ and reconciled with his sons
Daher al-Umar.fact: The backing of thousands of Metawali fighters significantly boosted Daher's military potential, and the Metawalis "remained faithful allies ... Daher was at the peak of his power, having consolidated his alliance with the Metawalis and reconciled with his sons.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: He possessed substantial financial resources, derived mainly from _____'s lucrative cotton trade, which he dominated during the preceding two decades
Daher al-Umar.fact: He possessed substantial financial resources, derived mainly from Acre's lucrative cotton trade, which he dominated during the preceding two decades.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher had lost his main allies in Constantinople: Ya'qub Agha was executed in the 1760s and Sulayman Agha died in _____
Daher al-Umar.fact: Daher had lost his main allies in Constantinople: Ya'qub Agha was executed in the 1760s and Sulayman Agha died in 1770. In September 1770, Uthman Pasha secured the appointment of his son, Darwish Pasha, as governor of Sidon, while recruiting the Shihabs as allies.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In September _____, Uthman Pasha secured the appointment of his son, Darwish Pasha, as governor of Sidon, while recruiting the Shihabs as allies
Daher al-Umar.fact: Daher had lost his main allies in Constantinople: Ya'qub Agha was executed in the 1760s and Sulayman Agha died in 1770. In September 1770, Uthman Pasha secured the appointment of his son, Darwish Pasha, as governor of Sidon, while recruiting the Shihabs as allies.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: While the war with _____ preoccupied Constantinople, Uthman Pasha was committed to eliminating Daher
Daher al-Umar.fact: While the war with Russia preoccupied Constantinople, Uthman Pasha was committed to eliminating Daher.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In October, _____ entered Palestine to make the dawra, the governor's annual tour to collect the miri taxes from his province, which funded the Hajj caravan
Daher al-Umar.fact: While the war with Russia preoccupied Constantinople, Uthman Pasha was committed to eliminating Daher. In September 1770, Uthman Pasha secured the appointment of his son, Darwish Pasha, as governor of Sidon, while recruiting the Shihabs as allies.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: He threatened to assault Acre, prompting Daher to strengthen its fortifications and arm every man in the city, Muslim and _____ alike
Daher al-Umar.fact: He threatened to assault Acre, prompting Daher to strengthen its fortifications and arm every man in the city, Muslim and Christian alike.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Political conditions favored the two leaders' cause, as the imperial government, bogged down in war with Russia, was ill positioned to confront a joint offensive by _____ and Daher
Daher al-Umar.fact: Political conditions favored the two leaders' cause, as the imperial government, bogged down in war with Russia, was ill positioned to confront a joint offensive by Ali Bey and Daher.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: His troops cleared _____'s subordinates from Gaza and Ramla without resistance, then together with Daher occupied Jaffa, giving them control over most of Palestine
Daher al-Umar.fact: In October, Uthman Pasha entered Palestine to make the dawra, the governor's annual tour to collect the miri taxes from his province, which funded the Hajj caravan. His troops cleared Uthman Pasha's subordinates from Gaza and Ramla without resistance, then together with Daher occupied Jaffa, giving them control over most of Palestine.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In late January _____, Ismail Bey rejected Daher's proposal to attack Uthman Pasha while he was leading the Hajj caravan citing risk of harm to the pilgrims
Daher al-Umar.fact: In late January 1771, Ismail Bey rejected Daher's proposal to attack Uthman Pasha while he was leading the Hajj caravan citing risk of harm to the pilgrims.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In the view of historian Abdul-_____, this represented Daher's failure to steer the campaign
Daher al-Umar.fact: In the view of historian Abdul-Karim Rafeq, this represented Daher's failure to steer the campaign.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: In early March, Daher and _____ set up headquarters at Muzayrib, a fort on the Hajj caravan road
Daher al-Umar.fact: In late January 1771, Ismail Bey rejected Daher's proposal to attack Uthman Pasha while he was leading the Hajj caravan citing risk of harm to the pilgrims. In early March, Daher and Ismail Bey set up headquarters at Muzayrib, a fort on the Hajj caravan road.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Whether due to the arrival of relief troops in _____ and/or another dispute over attacking Uthman Pasha in the presence of pilgrims, Daher and Ismail Bey decamped from Muzayrib
Daher al-Umar.fact: While waiting to intercept Uthman Pasha on his return from Mecca, Daher launched operations in Damascus province, sending his son Ahmad to capture Jabal Ajlun, other subordinates to collect taxes in the Jawlan, and his son Ali to raid the Nu'aym tribe in the Hauran. Whether due to the arrival of relief troops in Damascus and/or another dispute over attacking Uthman Pasha in the presence of pilgrims, Daher and Ismail Bey decamped from Muzayrib.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Ali Bey was nevertheless encouraged by his coalition's successes, dispatching reinforcements under his general Abu al-_____
Daher al-Umar.fact: Ali Bey was nevertheless encouraged by his coalition's successes, dispatching reinforcements under his general Abu al-Dhahab. On 6 June, Uthman Pasha fled and two days later, the Damascenes surrendered to Abu al-Dhahab.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: On 3 June, the rebel allies, with Daher's son Ali leading the vanguard, defeated _____ troops at Darayya and closed in on Damascus
Daher al-Umar.fact: On 3 June, the rebel allies, with Daher's son Ali leading the vanguard, defeated Ottoman troops at Darayya and closed in on Damascus.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: On 6 June, _____ fled and two days later, the Damascenes surrendered to Abu al-Dhahab
Daher al-Umar.fact: Whether due to the arrival of relief troops in Damascus and/or another dispute over attacking Uthman Pasha in the presence of pilgrims, Daher and Ismail Bey decamped from Muzayrib. On 6 June, Uthman Pasha fled and two days later, the Damascenes surrendered to Abu al-Dhahab.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: While most of their men were in _____, Daher and Nasif led a separate assault against Sidon, capturing the city on 11 June
Daher al-Umar.fact: On 3 June, the rebel allies, with Daher's son Ali leading the vanguard, defeated Ottoman troops at Darayya and closed in on Damascus. While most of their men were in Damascus, Daher and Nasif led a separate assault against Sidon, capturing the city on 11 June.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: On 18 June, Abu al-_____ surprised his allies and opponents alike by unilaterally withdrawing from Damascus
Daher al-Umar.fact: On 6 June, Uthman Pasha fled and two days later, the Damascenes surrendered to Abu al-Dhahab. On 18 June, Abu al-Dhahab surprised his allies and opponents alike by unilaterally withdrawing from Damascus.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: A chronicler of the period noted that the _____ were "completely astonished at this amazing event"
Daher al-Umar.fact: On 6 June, Uthman Pasha fled and two days later, the Damascenes surrendered to Abu al-Dhahab. A chronicler of the period noted that the Damascenes were "completely astonished at this amazing event".

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Rafeq holds these were contributing factors, but that Abu al-Dhahab's own ambitions to unseat _____ likely drove him to quit the campaign and return to Egypt
Daher al-Umar.fact: Rafeq holds these were contributing factors, but that Abu al-Dhahab's own ambitions to unseat Ali Bey likely drove him to quit the campaign and return to Egypt.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: The sudden turn of events and an attack by the Druze warriors of _____ compelled Daher and Nasif to quit Sidon on 20 June
Daher al-Umar.fact: The sudden turn of events and an attack by the Druze warriors of Yusuf Shihab compelled Daher and Nasif to quit Sidon on 20 June.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Darwish Pasha reentered Sidon and _____ returned to Damascus on 26 June
Daher al-Umar.fact: Darwish Pasha reentered Sidon and Uthman Pasha returned to Damascus on 26 June. By the end of August, Gaza and Ramla returned to Uthman Pasha's control, but Jaffa remained with Daher.

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Philipp comments that despite Daher's increased vulnerability, he "was actually able, after the withdrawal of the _____, to expand his realm as never before"
Daher al-Umar.fact: Philipp comments that despite Daher's increased vulnerability, he "was actually able, after the withdrawal of the Egyptians, to expand his realm as never before".

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations
Daher al-Umar.question: Daher captured Jaffa in August _____, fortifying and garrisoning it with 2,000 men, He took over the cotton-producing Bani Sa'b nahiye (centered around Qaqun)
Daher al-Umar.fact: Daher captured Jaffa in August 1771, fortifying and garrisoning it with 2,000 men, He took over the cotton-producing Bani Sa'b nahiye (centered around Qaqun).

Daher al-Umar.subject: International Relations

Exclusive economic zone.question: It stretches from the outer limit of the territorial sea at 12 nautical miles (_____; 14 mi) from the coast to 200 nautical miles (370 km; 230 mi) from the coast of the state in question
Exclusive economic zone.fact: An exclusive economic zone (EEZ), as prescribed by the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, is an area of the sea in which a sovereign state has exclusive rights regarding the exploration and use of marine resources, including energy production from water and wind.  It stretches from the outer limit of the territorial sea at 12 nautical miles (22 km; 14 mi) from the coast to 200 nautical miles (370 km; 230 mi) from the coast of the state in question.  It is also referred to as a maritime continental margin and, in colloquial usage, may include the continental shelf.  The term does not include either the territorial sea or the continental shelf beyond the 200 nautical mile limit.  The difference between the territorial sea and the exclusive economic zone is that the first confers full sovereignty over the waters, whereas the second is merely a "sovereign right" which refers to the coastal state's rights below the surface of the sea

The exception to this rule occurs when exclusive economic zones would overlap; that is, state coastal baselines are less than 400 nmi (741 km) apart. Financial Action Task Force.subject: International Relations
Financial Action Task Force.question: The FATF _____ is administratively hosted at the OECD in Paris, but the two organisations are separate
Financial Action Task Force.fact: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), also known by its French name, Groupe d'action financière (GAFI), is an intergovernmental organisation founded in 1989 on the initiative of the G7 to develop policies to combat money laundering and to maintain certain interest.  In 2001, its mandate was expanded to include terrorism financing.  The FATF Secretariat is administratively hosted at the OECD in Paris, but the two organisations are separate.  The objectives of FATF are to set standards and promote effective implementation of legal, regulatory and operational measures for combating money laundering, terrorist financing and other related threats to the integrity of the international financial system.  FATF is a "policy-making body" that works to generate the necessary political will to bring about national legislative and regulatory reforms in these areas.  FATF monitors progress in implementing its Recommendations through "peer reviews" ("mutual evaluations") of member countries

Financial Action Task Force.fact: In February 2012, the FATF codified its recommendations and Interpretive Notes into one document that maintains SR VIII (renamed Recommendation 8), and also includes new rules on weapons of mass destruction, corruption and wire transfers (Recommendation 16, commonly known as the "travel rule").  In October 2018, the FATF updated Recommendation No.  15, expanding its reach to include operations related to virtual assets.  It urged its member countries to ensure that providers of virtual asset services are regulated for AML/CFT objectives and licensed or registered.  Additionally, they should be under robust systems for supervision assurance and compliant with the FATF recommendations.  In June 2019, the FATF released its first guidance on the risk-based approach for virtual assets and virtual asset service providers.  This guidance offers recommendations on how member jurisdictions should regulate cryptocurrency businesses, placing anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) obligations on VAs and VASPs

It also extended Recommendation 16 to VASPs.  This guidance was updated on March 19 and October 2021.  ==== Forty recommendations on money laundering ==== The FATF's Forty Recommendations on Money Laundering of 1990 are the primary policies issued by FATF and the Nine Special Recommendations (SR) on Terrorism Financing (TF).
